animations.title: yourFAM drawing itself
animations.now: The tab's content nudges in (shared, 200ms), then /api/profile lands and the hub is rebuilt in one frame: an empty gold wash on first open, a silent rebuild every later time; pictures pop in.
animations.verdict: A many-times screen: redraws must hold still (Frequency, Tenth use). Paint what was seen last and reconcile only what changed (Doherty); an entrance only for content that truly arrives.
animations.notes:
Today openProfile -> setTab('profile') (the shared tab nudge on .screen-top and .scroll) and loadProfile -> fetch /api/profile?notes=1 -> renderProfile, which replaces #pfTop and #profileBody with innerHTML every time the tab is opened (16961). There is no cache, so the first open of a session shows the gold wash and the tab bar until the answer lands, then hero, numbers, buttons, interests and grid appear in one frame. Later opens rebuild the same DOM: the background-image spans of the grid are re-created, so tiles can flash, and nothing says what changed (a friend count after a follow-back, a vibe posted from the player). The grid tiles are backgrounds (.yf-pic-img), so the shared blur-up (seed-img only) never applies.
Option C keeps a device copy of the last /api/profile answer (localStorage, every read and write in try/catch; absent copy -> option B's path) and renders it on the tab's first frame. On the answer, diff by key: numbers (friends, vibes, mixes) roll only the digits that change (tabular-nums window, up when growing, 350ms IO), chained after any tile motion so one thing leads at a time (Staging); a name or place cross-fades 150ms; a new tile (key query+minutes or mix id) fades up 8px (260ms OUT, the owner's rail numbers); a gone tile exits 150ms IN to scale .92 and its siblings FLIP 250ms IO; interests enter/exit like changes-land. Nothing that did not change is touched, so the tenth open shows no motion at all.
Option A is the skill's entrance recipe; it must run once per session (track drawn keys like feedTopicsShown in arriveRails, 6270) or it fails Tenth use. Option B is exactly arriveRails' language applied to #yfGrid.
Interruptions: switching tab mid-entrance -> Motion.settle finishes it (fill none, so no state is held). The hub is live from frame one in all three; nothing waits on motion. Reduced motion: no entrance, no roll, values swap.
Shared parts not decided here: the tab nudge itself and picture blur-up (lead).

options.tradeoff: Reads as a page assembling, but only once a session; every later open must show nothing, or it fails the tenth use.

Hold 1.2s. Loop shows a second open: all at once, nothing moves.

animations.title: Vibes | Mixes shelf switch
animations.trigger: tap Vibes or Mixes, or the vibes/mixes number
animations.now: The copper underline jumps tab to tab and the grid's tiles are replaced in one frame; tapping the number also smooth-scrolls the grid into view (ignores reduced motion).
animations.verdict: A few-times switch that changes the whole grid: show which way you moved, as the app's own tabs do (§292), and keep it short. The underline should travel as one indicator.
animations.notes:
showProfileShelf toggles .on on two .yf-tab buttons (border-bottom 2px copper) and sets #yfGrid.innerHTML. The friend's page (showPersonShelf) is the same layout and should get the same motion. The stats buttons call it with scroll=true -> grid.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}), which should become 'auto' under reduced motion.
Option A reuses the owner's tab-switch numbers from Motion.screen 'tab' (6068: out 110ms, in 200ms after 90ms, 18px toward the new tab's side) on the grid only, with the old grid as an inert copy (absolute, over the new one) so the new tiles are live and tappable from frame one. dir = +1 going to Mixes (right), -1 to Vibes. The underline becomes one absolutely positioned 2px bar under the tabs moved by transform (translateX to the tab's left, scaleX for its width; the two tabs are equal, so translateX only) with a CSS transition - interruptible: a quick second tap turns it around from where it is. A second tap during the grid move finishes the first at once (the copy is removed), as Motion.settle does for screens.
Option B keeps the indicator and replaces the slide by a fade-up of the new tiles; option C follows the skill's frequency rule for tabs (no transition) and only fades the tab color.
Heights differ (5 vibes vs 1 mix): the scroll container simply takes the new height on frame one; nothing animates height. Empty shelf: the dashed note is one piece and moves like a tile.
Reduced motion: underline and grid change instantly (no 120ms crossfade - that rule is for screen changes).

options.name: Slide by side
options.summary: The underline glides to the tab; the grid nudges out the way you moved and the new tiles slide in
options.spec: bar 250ms IO translateX · out 110ms IN x→∓18 fade · in 200ms OUT x±18→0 +90ms
options.recipe: Exits + entrances; interruptibility (indicator on a transition)
options.tradeoff: Adds motion to every shelf switch; at 290ms it stays under the tenth-use bar but it is not free.
options.why: The owner's own tab-switch gesture (§292) reused, so a tab inside a page behaves like a tab of the app.
options.demoNote: Grid area of yourFAM: VIBES | MIXES labels with a 2px copper bar under VIBES; 3x2 vibe tiles below. t=0 tap MIXES: the bar glides right (250ms); vibe tiles slide 18px left and fade (110ms); t=90 two mix tiles ('Commute', 'Morning run', square covers) slide in from 18px right and fade in (200ms). Hold 1.2s. Tap VIBES: mirror image, moving left. Loop.

options.name: Tiles cascade
options.summary: The underline glides; the old tiles fade and the new ones rise one after another
options.spec: bar 250ms IO · old fade 120ms IN · tiles 260ms OUT y 8→0, 30ms apart, first 6
options.recipe: Entrances: split, then stagger (copies of one element)
options.tradeoff: Softer, but a cascade on every switch reads as loading, and it says nothing about direction.
options.demoNote: Same grid. t=0 tap MIXES: bar glides right (250ms); vibe tiles fade out (120ms); t=120 mix tiles rise 8px and fade in, 30ms apart, left to right (260ms each). Hold 1.2s; tap VIBES: same, bar glides left. Loop.

options.name: Instant, color only
options.summary: The grid changes on the next frame; only the tab label's color eases
options.spec: grid 0ms · tab color 150ms ease · underline jumps
options.tradeoff: Fastest and calmest; the switch stays as abrupt as today apart from the label color.
options.demoNote: Same grid. t=0 tap MIXES: underline jumps to MIXES, MIXES label darkens over 150ms, mix tiles are there on the next frame. Hold 1.2s; tap VIBES: same. Loop.

animations.title: Follow ⇄ Following
animations.trigger: tap Follow or Following (Friends list, a friend's profile)
animations.now: On tap the label becomes '✓ Following' and the button animates width old→new 260ms (.2,.8,.2,1); the tick draws 220ms after 80ms. Both states look alike. Friends redraws ~200ms later, tick gone.
animations.verdict: Keep the change-on-tap (§298) but stop animating width (Properties): hold the size, cross-fade the labels, give Following its own look, and never redraw the tick away.
animations.notes:
Motion.follow (6563) finds every button whose onclick contains followPerson('id'), swaps innerHTML and onclick, toggles .is-following (which has no CSS) and runs [{width: w0}, {width: w1}] for 260ms - a layout per frame, and in the centred .yf-acts row it drags the Message button with it. Then followPerson's success calls loadFriends -> renderFriends, which rebuilds the Friends rows with plain 'Following' (no tick), cutting both the width animation and the tick on a fast answer. On a friend's page nothing redraws, so the tick stays there - the two places disagree. Follow itself is gold at 19177 and 19209 but outline at 19167 and in personRow (18904).
Option A (async-button recipe): render both labels inside the button at all times, stacked in one grid cell (display:inline-grid; children grid-area:1/1), the button's width set by the wider ('✓ Following'); the inactive layer aria-hidden. A state change sets data-state; CSS transitions opacity+scale on both layers at once (150ms, leaving one to .9 on IN, arriving from .9 on OUT). Fill: Follow = copper with ink text, Following = outline (background-color 150ms). The tick path keeps pathLength=1 and draws by stroke-dashoffset 1->0, 220ms IO, 60ms after the tap. renderFriends must draw the same markup (tick included) so a redraw changes nothing visible.
Option B keeps the owner's 'takes its new width' look on transforms: the pill's paint lives on ::before, FLIP'd (scaleX from w0/w1 to 1, origin centre) while the label stays unscaled; neighbours FLIP too.
Option C keeps §298 literally and only fixes the redraw and the look.
Interrupt: a second tap mid-change re-targets the transitions (A, B) from where they are. Refusal: the same transition runs back, plus the server's sentence on the bottom line. Reduced motion: state changes on the frame (today Motion.follow already skips motion when !on()).

options.name: Hold size, swap labels

options.spec: labels 150ms cross-fade, scale .9↔1 · fill 150ms · tick 1→0 220ms IO +60ms · width fixed
options.tradeoff: 'Follow' sits in a button sized for 'Following' (about 22px of spare room on each side).
options.why: Same meaning as the owner's pick with no layout per frame; a fixed width means Message and the row's text never shift.
options.reduced: Label, fill and tick change on the frame.

Pill width unchanged (faint guide lines show both edges still). Hold 1s; tap again: reverse, no tick. Loop.

options.spec: pill ::before scaleX w0/w1→1 260ms IO, origin centre · labels 150ms · tick 220ms +80ms
options.tradeoff: Closest to §298; more parts (the label must not scale, neighbours must FLIP), and the row still changes size.
options.reduced: New width, label and tick on the frame.
options.demoNote: Same row. t=0 tap 'Follow': the copper pill's background stretches wider from its centre (260ms) as the label cross-fades to '✓ Following' and the fill fades to outline; the tick draws from t=80. Hold 1s; tap: it narrows back. Loop.

options.summary: Today's motion exactly, with the two fixes: Following gets its own look and the tick is never redrawn away

options.tradeoff: Animates width, which the skill forbids (layout every frame); on a long Friends list that is visible jank.

animations.title: A followed row finds its group
animations.trigger: follow or unfollow on Friends; the server answers
animations.now: When the server answers, the whole list is rebuilt: the row jumps from 'Follows you' to 'Friends' (or vanishes), group headers and '2 friends · 3 following' change in one frame.
animations.verdict: 'Where did they go?' is a real question here. Move the row to its new group (a spatial move) and roll the counts - or keep it still while you work down the list.
animations.notes:
renderFriends (18910) draws three groups - Friends, Following (one-way), Follows you - and nobody in two of them. A follow-back moves a person from Follows you to Friends (the group above); an unfollow of a friend moves them down to Follows you; an unfollow of a one-way row removes it from every group. Each happens when loadFriends answers (19001, 19013), by innerHTML, so the row teleports and the rows between shift by one row in the same frame. Group headers carry counts (<em>), and the top line carries three counts.
Option A: before the redraw, record each .fr-row's top by user id (a data-user attribute is needed: today the row only has the handle inside an onclick) and the header counts; redraw; then FLIP every row whose top changed (translateY from old-new to 0, 320ms IO, all together - one gesture), rows that left exit as inert copies (150ms IN, x -8, fade), new headers fade in 150ms. Counts roll only the changed digits (350ms IO, tabular-nums). The move starts when the server answers, from where the row was, so nothing is held; the button's tick keeps drawing inside the moving row. Rows are live during the move (transform only). A second follow mid-move: settle the first (cancel, rows land) then measure again.
Option B suits someone following back five people in a row: nothing moves under the thumb. The row's meta gains 'Friends now' (150ms fade); the regroup happens on the next open. Its cost: for a while the row sits under 'Follows you' while being a friend.
Option C reuses the §298 removal for the old place and the expander for the new one; two motions in two places split attention (Staging).
Search results (searchPeople) are not regrouped: they are a flat list. Reduced motion: list and counts update instantly.

options.name: Row travels to group
options.summary: When the server answers, the row glides up into Friends and the counts roll
options.spec: FLIP translateY 320ms IO(.77,0,.175,1) · then counts roll 350ms IO · leavers 150ms IN x−8
options.tradeoff: The list moves under the thumb for 320ms; following several in a row means aiming at a moving list.
options.why: Becoming friends is the moment this screen exists for; the row rising into Friends says it without words.
options.demoNote: Friends screen: top line '2 friends · 3 following · 4 followers'; FRIENDS header with Ana, Ben; FOLLOWS YOU header with Sam, Priya, Leo, each with a copper 'Follow'. t=0 tap Priya's Follow: label swaps to '✓ Following'. t=200 (server): Priya's row glides up into FRIENDS under Ben (320ms) as the FOLLOWS YOU header and Sam slide down one row; at t=520 '2 friends' rolls to '3', '3 following' to '4'. Hold 1.2s. Loop.

options.spec: no reorder · meta 'Friends now' fade 150ms · counts roll 350ms IO
options.tradeoff: Nothing moves under your thumb; until you come back, a friend sits under 'Follows you'.

options.tradeoff: Reuses the owner's removal look, but two motions in two places at once: the eye can follow only one.

animations.title: A friend's profile filling in
animations.now: The hero draws at once; when /api/person lands a numbers row (~60px) is inserted above Follow and Message, and the interests line and tiles appear below - all in one frame.
animations.verdict: A layout that changes shape when the fetch lands (Doherty). Reserve the rows from frame one so nothing jumps; let only the arriving values and tiles move.
animations.notes:
openPersonProfile pushes the screen (shared, 320ms) and calls renderFriendProfile(person) with no published data: the stats row is skipped (19144 'if(published)'), the interests line is skipped (interestLineHTML returns '' with no pills), the grid is empty (showPersonShelf returns early, 19236). When /api/person answers - often during or just after the push - everything is rebuilt by innerHTML: ~60px of numbers is inserted above the Follow and Message buttons (the interests line, under them at 19183, appears too), a ring may appear on the photo, the place prefix appears, tiles appear. A finger on its way to Follow lands on whatever slid under it.
Option A draws the stats row and the interests line on the first render with their final heights: numbers as an en dash in the same <b>, interests as three empty pill outlines at 40% opacity (or simply a reserved 35px line). animations.title: Removing a saved row
animations.trigger: tap a row's X in Save for Later or My Vibes
animations.now: Copy slides x 0→-45% and fades, 180ms (.4,0,1,1); then height, padding, margin →0 over 200ms. loadSaved then rebuilds the list (can cut the fold). 'Removed', no Undo. My Vibes: no motion.

removeSaved (21716) calls Motion.removeRow(row, row.remove, '#svBody .sv-row'): the real row leaves at once, an inert copy is put back in its place and slides out (180ms EASE_IN) then folds by animating height/padding/margin (200ms EASE, 180ms delay) - the forbidden properties - so every frame re-lays out the list. Then the DELETE's answer calls loadSaved -> renderSaved, which replaces #svBody.innerHTML: on a fast server (<380ms) the copy is destroyed mid-fold and the rows below jump. The bottom line says 'Removed' and nothing can undo it. My Vibes' X (18731) has none of this: it waits, reloads, redraws.
Option A keeps the owner's look: the copy is absolute (out of flow) and slides out; the rows below are FLIP'd: they are already in their new places on frame one and are translated down by the removed row's height, then glide to 0 (200ms IO) starting at 180ms - same timing as today, transforms only. The follow-up load must patch (by item id) or wait until the motion ends. Undo: the bottom line 'Removed · Undo' for at least 5s (the shared snack now gives 3500ms - needs the lead's change); the DELETE is sent when the line closes or the page is hidden (visibilitychange), so Undo only re-inserts locally (row fades back 200ms, rows below FLIP down 200ms IO). If the episode is on the player, setSaved(false) runs at the tap as today.
Option B adds the iOS gesture; it conflicts with the horizontal folder chips only if started on them, and with the edge back-swipe (start beyond 24px from the left edge).
Option C is the skill's plain exit: fade with an 8px nudge while the gap closes at the same time.
Last row removed: the empty-shelf sentence fades in (150ms) where the list was. Reduced motion: row gone, list closed instantly; the Undo line still appears (it is information, not motion).

animations.title: Deleting a vibe from your grid
animations.trigger: hold your tile 500ms, then 'Remove vibe from profile'
animations.now: Hold: the squeeze holds, a 10ms buzz at 500ms, the sheet. After the server answers the grid is rebuilt: the tile vanishes, later tiles jump a cell; the 'N vibes' number stays stale.
animations.verdict: Remove on confirm, let the tile recede and the grid close over it (FLIP), roll the vibes number down. Optionally let the hold show that it is counting.
animations.notes:
armVibeHolds (17504) arms a 500ms timer per own tile; the shared squeeze holds the tile at ~0.947 meanwhile, navigator.vibrate(10) fires, openVibeTileMenu shows the shared action sheet with one red action. deleteMyVibe (17548) sends DELETE /api/vibe and only on success splices profileVibes, re-renders #yfGrid (showProfileShelf), shows 'Vibe deleted', reloads the circle and calls loadProfileQuietly - which never redraws the hub, so the 'N vibes' number is stale (bug). Tiles after the deleted one shift a cell; at a row end the next tile jumps up and to the far left. The same delete from a post's menu (19691) re-renders all posts (renderVibePosts) and from My Vibes (18731) waits and reloads.
Option A: on confirm, before the request, record tile rects (key query+minutes), splice, re-render, put an inert copy of the tile where it was (absolute in the grid) and run scale 1->.92 + opacity 1->0, 150ms IN; FLIP every later tile from old rect to new (translate, 250ms IO, 30ms apart, first 6, the rest with the sixth); the vibes <b> rolls down (350ms IO). Posts and My Vibes use the saved-remove choice (rows), not this grid motion.
Option B adds hold progress, the hold-to-confirm case the skill times as linear: after the 90ms squeeze, the tile keeps sinking .95->.92 and a black veil rises 0->30% over the remaining 410ms, cancelled with the timer (10px move or lift). It must stay below the 'many' bar: the hold is rare.
Option C uses the §298 slide-left for the tile; in a 3-column grid the copy slides over its left neighbour.

animations.title: Choosing your five interests
animations.trigger: tap an interest chip in Edit profile; type one and add
animations.now: Each tap rebuilds the chips: a chosen chip fills copper and gains a check, growing ~18px so the wrap reflows; '3 OF 5' swaps; at five the rest dim and a tap on one does nothing.
animations.verdict: Did my tap register, and how many are left? Keep each chip's width, swap the icon in place, roll the count; a refused tap at five earns one small shake of the counter.
animations.notes:
renderIdentityInterests replaces #identityIntChips.innerHTML on every toggle (20022). A chosen .yf-int prepends a 13px check (yfIcon('check')) and gets bold: the chip widens ~18px and every chip after it can wrap to another line in the same frame - the chip you tapped may even move away from your finger. #identityIntCount text swaps. At the maximum, unchosen chips get .dim and toggleIdentityInterest returns silently (20038). A typed interest is pushed to the end of the list and chosen if there is room (20044) - it appears in one frame, possibly off screen.
Option A: give every chip a fixed 14px icon slot (unchosen: a '+' at 60% opacity; chosen: the check), font weight unchanged (a bold switch also changes width - use color only), so width never changes. Update the tapped chip in place (class + aria-pressed), not by rebuilding. The two icons are both present, stacked; the icon-swap recipe without Motion: cross-fade with scale .3<->1 and blur 3px<->0 over 300ms cubic-bezier(.25,.1,0,1). Fill is a color transition (150ms). The count is a one-digit roll (300ms IO; up when adding). At five, the others' dimming is a 150ms color fade; a tap on a dim chip shakes #identityIntCount (translateX 0,-10,10,-6,6,-3,0 over 360ms) - the skill's failed-attempt exaggeration - and nothing else. A typed chip enters at the end with scale .95->1 + fade (200ms OUT) and is scrolled into view if needed.
Option B floods the fill from the tap point (clip-path circle on a ::before), a richer 'did it register'.
Option C is the frequency answer (instant), still with the reserved slot (the reflow is the real problem).
Interrupt: transitions re-target on a quick second tap. Reduced motion: icon, fill and count change instantly; no shake (the dim chips and the count already say why).

options.tradeoff: Unchosen chips gain a faint '+', a small change to the design.
options.why: Nothing reflows under the finger, the count shows five filling up, and the one refusal explains itself without a toast.
options.reduced: Icon, fill and count change instantly; no shake.

animations.title: Opening Edit profile
animations.trigger: tap Edit profile, or a Settings editor row; X or Save
animations.now: Edit profile, Where you are and Your interests (from Settings) are shown with showScreen and no 'how': they appear and leave in one frame, while every other door here pushes in (320/260ms).
animations.verdict: Rare, so it may move. These editors close with an X, so they should behave like the app's sheets (fade and lift), one motion for all three.
animations.notes:
openIdentity('edit') ends in showScreen('identity') with no kind (20170); closeIdentity and the edit Save return with showScreen(identityReturn) (20273, 20347). The same is true of the location editor (18590, 18595) and the interests editor opened from Settings (18641). They are not on the navigation stack (the intro-not-on-stack rule), and they show an X in the top-left (.sheet-close), not the back chevron - so they read as modal pages. Motion.screen returns early with no 'how' (6022), hence the snap. In first-run mode identity and intro are sign-up steps and keep the shared 'step' motion; this entry is only for their editor mode.
Option A adds a Motion.screen kind 'sheet': the arriving editor animates opacity 0->1 and translateY 14px->0 over 200ms OUT (the owner's sheet numbers, mo-in/mo-lift at 2116), the page beneath stays still; closing, the editor is kept as .leaving on-top (inert, as screens already are) and drops 8px while fading (150ms IN), the page beneath already active. The fixed parts (tab bar, mini player) of the page beneath never move. Kind passed by openIdentity/openLocationFromSettings/openInterestsFromSettings and their closers.
Option B is the iOS full-height page sheet: bigger travel, the page beneath scales to .97 and dims; out 220ms.
Option C changes the X into a back chevron and puts the editors on the push/pop motion (navigate/goBack) - which would touch the not-on-stack rule; 'return by name' can still be kept with the push motion passed explicitly.
Save: the editor leaves the same way as X; what changed on the hub is the changes-land entry. Reduced motion: the app's rule for a screen change (120ms crossfade) applies to all three.

animations.title: Your changes landing on yourFAM
animations.trigger: Save in Edit profile or in the photo editor
animations.now: After Save the hub is fetched and rebuilt: the new photo, name and pills appear in one frame. A new photo waits for the server's image check (can take seconds) with the old one showing, then pops.
animations.verdict: What changed? Answer it on the page: the photo cross-fades, new pills arrive, removed ones recede. Show the new photo at once and say it is being checked.

The photo path: savePhotoCrop closes the editor (shared modal fade) and saveAvatar POSTs /api/me with the data URL; the server checks the photo with its image check (§224) before answering, then loadProfile (on the hub) or drawIdentityPicture (on Edit profile) swaps it in and 'Picture saved' shows. Until then the old photo stays, with nothing saying anything is happening. Option A: keep the old hub nodes until the answer, then patch in place. Photo: put the new over the old one in one isolated wrapper (isolation:isolate; both mix-blend-mode:plus-lighter), opacities 1->0 and 0->1 over 300ms cubic-bezier(.25,.1,0,1), so the midpoint is never washed out (cross-fades recipe). For the avatar, show the local crop immediately (optimistic, only on this device) with 'Checking photo…' (Geist Mono 9px, under the photo); on success the line fades (150ms); on refusal the photo cross-fades back and the server's sentence is the bottom line. Name/place: text cross-fade 150ms. Interests (by id): new pills scale .95->1 + fade 200ms OUT, 40ms apart; removed pills fade 150ms IN; the line's other pills FLIP 200ms IO. Option B reuses the §298 blur-up (Motion.picture's frames: blur 8->0, scale 1.06->1, fade, 320ms) for the new photo - but blur-up means 'arrived from the network'. Option C is instant with the status line. Same for Edit profile's own 78px circle (drawIdentityPicture). Reduced motion: everything swaps; the 'Checking photo…' line still shows (information).

animations.title: Putting a row in a folder
animations.trigger: folder icon on a row → pick a folder in the sheet
animations.now: The sheet closes, the server answers, the shelf is rebuilt: the row's meta gains '· Commute' and the chip count goes 2→3 in one frame. With a folder chosen, a row moved away just vanishes.
animations.verdict: 'Where did it go?' The app already answers that for the queue: the picture arcs to where it went and the count bumps (§292). Reuse it for folders.
animations.notes:
chooseFolderFor (21695) opens the shared action sheet listing the kind's folders; fileInFolder posts and, on success, toasts 'Moved to …' and reloadShelf -> loadSaved/loadMyVibe -> full rebuild. Folder chips (21608) are a sideways-scrolling row at the top: All, each folder with its count in a <span>, '+ New folder'. With a folder picked, the list is filtered (shelfFilter), so moving a row elsewhere removes it from view.
Option A, drawn over a change already made: on the sheet item, update locally first (row.folder_id, the chip counts, the meta) and re-render in place; then fly a 38x38 copy of the row's play square (.sv-art) from its rect to the chip's centre on an arc (the techniques' arc(): x linear, y lifted by sin(pi t) x 15% of the distance), 380ms IO, scale 1->1.15 at the top->.4 at the end, fade over the last 30%, with a soft shadow on ::after that fades in at the top (the 'lift' recipe). On landing, the chip's count digit rolls (300ms IO) and the chip bumps 1->1.1->1 (220ms) - the queue's language (toQueue, 6288: arc 450ms + badge bump 260ms). If the chip is outside the chips row's scroll view, scroll it in first (scrollIntoView inline:'nearest', smooth unless reduced) and fly after 200ms. A row leaving a filtered view: the row's copy slides toward the chip row (up 8px + fade, 150ms IN) and the rows below FLIP up 200ms IO. Refused: re-render, bottom line. 'New folder' from the sheet: the new chip scales .95->1 + fades (200ms OUT) before the flight lands in it.
Option B stays where you look: the meta label wipes in like the writer's title (§298, clip-path inset, 320ms).
Option C is today plus optimism. Picking a folder chip (filter) stays instant: it is a filter, used like tabs. Reduced motion: meta and counts update instantly.

animations.title: Turning a setting on or off
animations.now: Nine toggles are rows with a chevron, like rows that open screens; a tap rebuilds the whole list and 'Off' becomes 'On' in one frame; most add a bottom line.
animations.verdict: A toggle should look like one (Jakob, Similarity), and its thumb should travel on a transition - updated in place, so it can turn around - not by rebuilding the list.
animations.notes:
settingsRow (18315) draws every row the same: label, value text, chevron. The toggles are Dark mode, Keep the voice's pitch, Big stories, Your teams' final scores, Say 'Hey FAM', Send my questions to AI (asks first), Count me in FAM's totals, Private search, Show my name. Each handler ends in renderSettings/refreshSettingsIfOpen, a full innerHTML rebuild, so no transition can run, and a tap during a late rebuild can be lost.
Option A: a settingsSwitch(label, on, action) row: no chevron; on the right the existing .mix-switch markup (44x24 track, 18px thumb, 20px travel - it lives at 1802 for the mix's private switch), with role='switch' and aria-checked on the row (the whole row stays the target). The handler flips the row's class and aria in place (optimistic) and calls the server; a refusal flips it back with the server's sentence. Thumb: transform translateX 0<->20px, transition 200ms IO; track background-color 150ms ease. Because it is a transition, a second tap mid-way turns it around from where it is. Note .mix-switch today uses bare 'ease' at 160ms on a moving thumb - the same tokens should serve both. Dark mode: the control is this switch; the page's own color change is the theme-switch item (lead: transitions off for the frame the theme changes, so the thumb should move after it, or simply land). 'Send my questions to AI' opens a confirm first: the switch moves only on the answer.
Option B keeps the words and rolls them in a 1-line window (the numbers recipe applied to a two-state word).
Option C: no motion, but still in place (no rebuild).
Reduced motion: thumb and color jump.

animations.title: Adding to your story
animations.trigger: tap (+) on your photo; X; Post
animations.now: The dark editor appears in one frame over yourFAM; tool panels pop in and out; Post closes it in one frame, the line says 'Added to your story', and the ring appears on your photo unseen.
animations.verdict: Rare, and this page's peak: it may be choreographed (each move ≤450ms). Grow it out of the (+) as stories grow out of faces (§298), and show the post going into your ring.
animations.notes:
The (+) badge on your hero photo (17378, 24px) and your photo itself when no story is up call openNoteComposer (9400), which sets #vibeComposer.hidden=false (9414): a full-screen dark editor (canvas with a sunset background, Text/Stickers/Background/Speak down the right, caption box, 'Your story' and the copper arrow). Tool panels (#vcsPanel) toggle hidden (9537). X: hidden=true. Post (postNoteStory, 9905): on success closeVibeComposer, snack 'Added to your story · View', then loadProfileQuietly -> renderProfile, which draws the copper ring (.yf-photo-btn.ring) around your photo - unseen, a fetch later. The same editor serves VIBE! from the player (openVibeComposer); the open/close choice here should apply there too (origin: the VIBE! button).
Opening (A and B): Motion.growStory's approach (6445): clip-path circle(r at the (+)'s centre) -> circle(cover), 300ms OUT; closing: an inert copy shrinks back into the (+) (240ms IN) - the owner's story pick (§298). Tool panels: drawer recipe from the bottom (translateY 100%->0, 280ms OUT; out 200ms IN), kept mounted and inert while closed.
B's post storyboard (rare: the skill allows choreography), drawn over the change already made: on the server's OK, set your story locally (myStoryPerson) and render the ring at once; then 0ms: an inert copy of the canvas shrinks to your photo's rect (translate + scale, border-radius 18px->50%, 380ms IO) and fades over its last 20%; 380ms: an SVG circle laid on the ring draws (stroke-dashoffset 1->0 with pathLength 1, rotated -90deg so it starts at 12 o'clock, 400ms IO), removed at the end so the real ring remains; 780ms: the bottom line. If the editor was opened from dailyFAM's row, the target is #yfMyRing; if no face is on screen, the copy just fades (150ms).
C is the sheet recipe for the whole editor. Reduced motion: shown/hidden instantly; the ring is simply there; the line shows.
